methods: To examine the mismatch between contemporaneous screening and the six-hour target, a separate training-only diagnostic paired $x(t)$ with $\mathrm{tp}(t+6\,\mathrm{h})$. Contemporaneous correlations use 18,410 training timestamps; lead-time and rank-partial correlations use 18,409 pairs, excluding the last training origin so that its target does not cross the training boundary. These are distinct from the 18,404 windowed training targets. Rank-partial correlations correlate residuals after regressing the ranks of each predictor and the future target on the rank of current precipitation, $\mathrm{tp}(t)$, with an intercept. They control only current precipitation and establish neither causality nor independent model-based predictive contribution. Pointwise 95\% percentile intervals use moving blocks of 28 consecutive six-hourly pairs (seven days), 2,000 replicates and seed 42, with common sampled indices across variables. The original 11-variable pool comprises u10, v10, d2m, t2m, sp, e, mxtpr, mntpr, tcc, ssr and lsp; the expanded pool adds grid-cell wind speed, spatially averaged as ws, and untruncated $\mathrm{cp}=\mathrm{tp}-\mathrm{lsp}$. Within each pool and replicate, candidates are ranked by absolute lead-time correlation. Selection frequency is the fraction entering the top seven; complete-set stability is the fraction whose unordered top-seven set equals the original set. Supplementary Tables~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_associations} and~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_selection_stability} report the separate diagnostics.
controlled: The saved q21 C6 comparison replaces d2m with cp in the original seven-predictor C0 configuration. Within each architecture, C0 and C6 use the same seven-variable budget, six-snapshot window, hyperparameters, chronological 70/15/15 split, training-only scaling and five seeds (42, 123, 7, 2024 and 99), evaluated on the same 3,939 test targets. Unlike the untruncated cp in the correlation diagnostic, C6 uses cp truncated to non-negative values at each grid cell before spatial averaging; the diagnostic intervals and selection frequencies are not transferred to that processed variable. Paired differences are C6 minus C0 seed-level RMSE, averaged over seeds, not RMSE differences of averaged predictions. Pointwise 95\% seed-t intervals use four degrees of freedom; separate moving-block percentile intervals use 28 consecutive test targets, 5,000 replicates and seed 42, resampling the full series jointly across seeds and configurations before applying subset masks. The latter describe test-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted runs, whereas seed-t intervals describe variability across the five matched refits; neither is adjusted for multiple comparisons. Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_c6} provides both.
results1: The six-hour lead-time correlations of mxtpr, mntpr and lsp fell to 0.515, 0.525 and 0.530, respectively, from contemporaneous values of approximately 0.90--0.99, close to the precipitation-persistence association of 0.525. After controlling only current precipitation, rank-partial correlations were 0.251 for tcc, $-0.188$ for sp, 0.186 for v10 and $-0.024$ for mxtpr (Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_associations}). Within the original 11-variable pool, lead-time screening retained the original seven predictors, and the complete set was recovered in 99.7\% of 2,000 bootstrap replicates (unrounded fraction 0.9965). Within the expanded 13-variable pool, cp entered and d2m exited; complete-set recovery was 0\%, and v10 entered the top seven in 79.7\% of replicates (Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_selection_stability}). The stability statements are conditional on their respective candidate pools.
results2: Replacing d2m with the processed cp in C6 did not improve overall RMSE under the matched settings. For XGBoost, the mean paired difference was $+0.000132$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ ($+0.054\%$), with seed-t and moving-block intervals of $[-0.000776,+0.001040]$ and $[-0.001366,+0.001613]$~mm\,h$^{-1}$. For BiLSTM-Attention it was $+0.001113$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ ($+0.458\%$), with intervals of $[+0.000592,+0.001633]$ and $[+0.000095,+0.002119]$~mm\,h$^{-1}$; all five seeds had higher RMSE. The wet and upper-tail BiLSTM-Attention seed-t intervals included zero despite positive sampling intervals, so the overall result is not extended to every subset (Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_c6}). These tests support retaining the original local seven-variable configuration under the tested conditions, not the optimality of contemporaneous screening or of the predictor set.
discussion: Contemporaneous association is not six-hour predictive contribution, and a rank-partial association does not demonstrate a causal effect or a gain in model performance. The candidate-pool dependence and matched C6 results in Section~\ref{sec:predictor_selection_results} therefore qualify the original screening rationale. A separate, pre-specified q21 configuration, C3, added upstream U1 inputs (the original seven variables plus ws, averaged over 52.75--53.75$^\circ$N, 10.5--7.0$^\circ$W) and U2 inputs (500-hPa geopotential and total-column water vapour, cosine-latitude weighted over 50--57$^\circ$N, 20--7$^\circ$W). Overall RMSE decreased by 6.4\% for XGBoost and 7.0\% for BiLSTM-Attention. C3 expands both spatial coverage and the predictor count from seven to 17, so it is not a controlled seven-variable selection comparison. C3a (U1 only, 15 predictors) and C3b (U2 only, nine predictors) were added after inspecting C3 and are exploratory. Their results are reported separately in Supplementary Tables~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_upstream_xgboost} and~\ref{supp-stab:r2m3_upstream_bilstm_attn}. These spatial sensitivity tests show that the local configuration can omit useful upstream information; they do not establish a uniquely best selection strategy.
limitation: The feature-selection evidence is restricted to the tested candidate pools, two retrained architectures and one chronological split. The untruncated-cp screening and cellwise-truncated-cp C6 test are related but not identical variable definitions. The original local predictor set can be retained within these comparisons, but cannot be claimed to be globally optimal; upstream sensitivity also limits conclusions based solely on local marginal rankings.
